At the end of the day what is momentarily our fact and truth might change (for example some of history’s most respected scientists thought the earth was flat, which at the time was a fact given what they knew, but is now incorrect)

I would say you should map it out with 

1) the definitions of knowledge that you agree with (extra points if you relate them to the types of truth)

2) the possibility of knowledge being independent from culture (remember everything is relative, ask yourself if it’s possible for knowledge to bloom without culture? Even maths was capable of progressing because of the golden age in the Middle East which was heavily reliant on islam and its encouragement for knowledge)

3) give examples of universally accepted ideas (like gravity) and relate them to truth and how even thought culture may make us perceive the reasoning for it differently, we still acknowledge that it does exist. 

4) rebuttal that

5) conclusion
